You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Calling Flush on the ETag response writer sends buffered bytes to the client before the response is complete, so the ETag can no longer be set (the request says Flush must not bypass the buffer).

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Hijack after a buffered write drops the response. Handler does `WriteHeader(201)`, `Write("PREFIX")`, then `http.NewResponseController(w).Hijack()` and writes `RAW`. Over a raw TCP socket, ETag(h) emits only `RAW\r\n`. Stdlib, same handler without ETag, emits `HTTP/1.1 201 Created\r\nX-A: 1\r\n...\r\n\r\nRAW\r\n`. Cause: `Hijack` sets `streaming = true` without calling `start()`, so the status, headers and buffered bytes are never written. Criterion 9 requires the buffered response to be sent on this path. The existing Hijack test (etag_test.go ~L504) only hijacks without writing first, so it cannot catch this.
- [minor] `Compress(ETag(h))` (ETag inside Compress) sends a gzip body with an ETag that is the hash of the plain bytes, not the encoded bytes. Not reproduced as a correctness failure: the 304 round trip succeeds. The doc only says what happens outside Compress and is silent on this ordering, which is a doc gap.
- [minor] A handler that calls `WriteHeader(103)` after `Flush` has the 103 silently dropped (`code=200 body="ab"`). A 1xx after final headers is invalid HTTP, so this is probably acceptable; the criterion's "forwarded immediately" wording is not met in this case.
- [minor] `WriteHeader(0)` does not panic in the handler's call stack. It panics later, in `finish`, with "invalid WriteHeader code 0". Stdlib panics at the call site. Net effect is similar under net/http's recovery.
- [minor] Headers set after `Write` are applied, because the header map is read at `finish` time. Stdlib ignores them. Not reproduced as a criterion failure; undocumented.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
Fix round for /tmp/ff-eval-gi63dkm2/workspace middleware/etag.go (+ etag_test.go). Only touch those two files.

GOAL: Fix the reviewer's blocking finding and two small items without changing other behavior.

FILES: middleware/etag.go (etagResponseWriter.Hijack, WriteHeader, the ETag doc comment), middleware/etag_test.go.

CONSTRAINTS: stdlib only; keep the existing tests passing; keep the error strings.

Fixes:
1. [blocking] Hijack after a buffered write drops the response. Repro: handler does `w.Header().Set("X-A","1")`, `WriteHeader(201)`, `Write("PREFIX")`, then `http.NewResponseController(w).Hijack()` and writes `RAW` to the conn. Without ETag, net/http sends `HTTP/1.1 201 Created ... X-A: 1 ... PREFIX` before handing over the connection; with ETag only `RAW` arrives. Fix: in Hijack, when the underlying writer is a Hijacker, if the handler already called WriteHeader or Write (wroteHeader true) and we are not already streaming, call start() (sending status, headers and buffered bytes unchanged, no ETag) before delegating; if nothing was written, send nothing (as today). Then mark streaming. Add a test using a real httptest.NewServer and a raw net.Dial TCP request that asserts the 201 status line, the X-A header, PREFIX and RAW all arrive, and the existing no-write hijack test still passes.
2. Doc comment: add that placed inside Compress (Compress(ETag(h))) ETag hashes the uncompressed bytes. Keep the existing sentences.
3. WriteHeader with an invalid code (< 100 or > 999) panics at the call site with the same message net/http uses: fmt.Sprintf("invalid WriteHeader code %v", code). Add a test.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. `middleware.ETag` has type `func(http.Handler) http.Handler` and a doc comment that says it buffers the full GET/HEAD response in memory, and notes that placed outside Compress it hashes the encoded bytes, and that NoCache strips If-None-Match so 304s never happen behind it.
2. GET/HEAD, handler responds 200 (explicit WriteHeader(200) or implicit via Write, or writes nothing at all) without an ETag header → response carries a strong ETag `"<hex digest of body>"` (quoted, no W/ prefix), identical bytes give identical ETags, different bytes give different ETags, and the body is delivered unchanged.
   Hostile: handler writes in many small chunks (same ETag as one write); empty body; body larger than 1 MiB.
3. Handler set its own ETag (strong or weak) → middleware never overwrites it.
4. If-None-Match matches the response's ETag (generated or handler-set) on a 200 GET/HEAD → status 304, no body, ETag header kept, Cache-Control/Vary/Expires/Last-Modified-free headers kept as stdlib does; Content-Type, Content-Length and Content-Encoding removed (as stdlib writeNotModified does; also drop Last-Modified when ETag present like stdlib).
5. Matching follows RFC 9110 §13.1.2: weak comparison (`W/"x"` matches `"x"` and vice versa, both weak match), comma-separated lists with optional whitespace (OWS) around members, multiple If-None-Match header lines are all considered, and `*` matches any 200 response.
   Hostile: an entity-tag containing a comma, e.g. If-None-Match `"a,b"` must match ETag `"a,b"` and `"a"` must NOT match it (no naive strings.Split on comma); malformed members (unquoted `abc`, unterminated `"abc`, empty header, lone `,`) never produce a match and never panic; `"x"` must not match `"xy"`; case matters (`w/"x"` is not a weak tag).
6. HEAD where the handler wrote no body bytes: do NOT generate an ETag (the empty-body hash would be wrong for the GET representation); a handler-set ETag is still matched for 304. HEAD with a body written by the handler gets the ETag of that body.
7. Other methods (POST, PUT, DELETE, ...) are not buffered at all: the handler gets the original ResponseWriter or an unbuffered pass-through, no ETag added, If-None-Match ignored, streaming/Flush works immediately.
8. Non-200 final statuses (201, 204, 206, 301, 404, 500, and a 304 the handler itself sends) pass through unchanged: same status, headers, body; no ETag added; no 304 conversion even if If-None-Match matches a handler-set ETag.
   Hostile: WriteHeader called twice (first wins, like net/http); 1xx informational WriteHeader (e.g. 103 Early Hints) is forwarded immediately to the underlying writer and is NOT taken as the final status.
9. The buffering writer forwards optional interfaces like compressResponseWriter: `Unwrap()` returns the underlying writer (so http.NewResponseController works); `Hijack` delegates or returns the "chi/middleware: http.Hijacker is unavailable on the writer" error; `Push` likewise with the Pusher error; `Flush` (from the handler, via http.Flusher or ResponseController) stops buffering: writes the status, headers and buffered bytes unchanged WITHOUT adding an ETag or doing 304, then streams subsequent writes directly and flushes the underlying writer. A response flushed this way must not be double-written at the end.
10. Tests in middleware/etag_test.go cover every criterion and hostile input above; README has the row and link; `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` pass and `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.

CHECKS: while working `go test -race -count=1 -run ETag ./middleware`; at the end `go clean -testcache && go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (empty).
